test_cases.title: Every table's column type, nullability, and unique constraints match PRD §8.4 fixture
test_cases.given: the SQLAlchemy models and a structured PRD §8.4 fixture (JSON/YAML) enumerating every table's fields

test_cases.then: each column's type, nullability, default, and unique constraint on the live model matches the fixture entry

Base.metadata is importable without a live DB connection

For each table in the fixture, resolve the matching SQLAlchemy model via Base.registry
For each field, compare fixture type/nullable/default/unique against `Column.type`, `Column.nullable`, `Column.default`, `Column.unique`/`UniqueConstraint`

test_cases.title: Fixture-driven model test fails when a field is deliberately mismatched
test_cases.given: the same PRD §8.4 fixture used by TC-02
test_cases.when: a model field is deliberately mutated to diverge from the fixture (e.g. a nullable column flipped to NOT NULL)
test_cases.then: the fixture-driven assertion fails, proving the gate actually detects divergence rather than passing vacuously
test_cases.objective: Prove TC-02's assertion mechanism is not a no-op — it fails on a real mismatch.
preconditions: Test harness allows monkeypatching a single model column for the duration of one test
steps: Monkeypatch `usage_events.session_id` to `nullable=True` (fixture declares `nullable=False`)
Re-run the TC-02 comparison logic against the mutated model
expected_results: The comparison raises an assertion failure identifying `usage_events.session_id` as mismatched
Monkeypatch is reverted after the test (no cross-test leakage)

test_cases.title: downgrade(base) -> upgrade(head) round trip produces an identical schema
test_cases.given: the migration chain has been applied to a disposable test database
test_cases.when: alembic downgrade base is run followed by alembic upgrade head
test_cases.then: both commands complete with no errors and the resulting schema is identical to the first apply
test_cases.objective: Verify migration reversibility: every revision's downgrade() cleanly reverts and re-upgrading reproduces the exact same schema (AC2, C-4).
preconditions: Disposable test Postgres instance
Migration chain already applied once (first apply snapshot captured)
steps: Run `alembic upgrade head`; snapshot table/column/constraint/index set via SQLAlchemy inspector
Run `alembic downgrade base`
Run `alembic upgrade head` again; snapshot the schema a second time
Diff the two snapshots
expected_results: Both alembic commands exit 0
Second snapshot's table/column/constraint/index set is identical to the first (empty diff)

test_cases.title: Round-trip test fails a revision whose downgrade() is a no-op or missing
test_cases.given: a deliberately broken revision whose downgrade() body is `pass` (does not drop what upgrade() created)
test_cases.when: the TC-04 round-trip test is run against that revision in isolation
test_cases.then: the round-trip assertion fails, proving the gate catches a non-working downgrade rather than passing vacuously
test_cases.objective: Prove the round-trip check in test_migrations.py detects a broken downgrade(), not just a well-behaved one.
preconditions: A throwaway test revision with `downgrade(): pass` added to an isolated test migrations directory
steps: Apply the throwaway revision with `alembic upgrade head`
Run `alembic downgrade base`
Reflect the schema and compare against the pre-upgrade (empty) state
expected_results: Post-downgrade schema still contains objects the no-op downgrade() failed to drop
The round-trip assertion raises a failure identifying the leftover objects

test_cases.title: alembic check detects an intentionally introduced model/migration drift

test_cases.then: it reports a non-empty diff, proving the gate actually detects drift rather than always reporting clean

Run `alembic check` against that database using the drifted model metadata
expected_results: Command exits non-zero or raises

test_cases.title: Duplicate (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts) insert into usage_events violates the unique constraint
test_cases.given: the usage_events table exists with a unique constraint on (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts)
test_cases.when: two rows are inserted with the same (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts)
test_cases.then: the second insert raises an IntegrityError/unique-violation rather than creating a duplicate row
test_cases.objective: Verify the idempotency-foundation unique constraint (A-002, NFR-012 foundation) rejects duplicate ingest writes at the DB layer.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events table empty
steps: Insert a usage_events row with test_data values
Attempt to insert a second row with the identical (program_id, session_id, cmd_ts)
expected_results: First insert succeeds
Second insert raises a unique-constraint IntegrityError
usage_events contains exactly one row for that key tuple after the attempted duplicate

test_cases.title: usage_events accepts rows sharing program_id/session_id when cmd_ts differs
test_cases.given: an existing usage_events row for a given (program_id, session_id)
test_cases.when: a second row is inserted with the same program_id and session_id but a different cmd_ts
test_cases.then: the insert succeeds, proving the unique constraint is scoped to the full 3-column tuple and not overly broad
test_cases.objective: Verify the unique constraint does not falsely reject legitimate distinct events within the same session.
preconditions: Disposable test database migrated to head
usage_events table empty
steps: Insert a usage_events row with cmd_ts_1
Insert a second usage_events row with the same program_id/session_id but cmd_ts_2
expected_results: Both inserts succeed with no constraint violation
usage_events contains 2 distinct rows for the (program_id, session_id) pair

test_cases.title: Migration failure surfaces via structlog JSON, not a raw traceback
test_cases.given: a migration run that is forced to fail (e.g. applying a revision against a database already partially migrated in a conflicting state)
test_cases.when: alembic upgrade is invoked and the failure occurs
test_cases.then: the failure is surfaced as a structlog JSON log entry via app/core/logging.py's formatter, with alembic_version left at the last successfully applied revision, rather than an unstructured raw traceback
test_cases.objective: Verify migration failures are observable via the project's structured JSON logging (NFR-011), per the story's observability assumption.
preconditions: Disposable test database
A deliberately conflicting migration state set up to force a failure
structlog configured per app/core/logging.py

test_data.forced_conflict: duplicate index name collision on second upgrade attempt

steps: Set up a database state that will cause the target revision's upgrade() to raise
Run `alembic upgrade head` capturing log output
Inspect captured log output and the resulting alembic_version row
expected_results: A structlog JSON-formatted error log entry is emitted describing the failure
No unstructured raw Python traceback is the sole failure signal in captured output
alembic_version still reflects the last successfully applied revision, not the failed one
